title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - A-8
notes:
West leads the ♣Q against 7NT. Outside of spades there are 8 top tricks (4 hearts, 2 diamonds, and 2 clubs). After winning the opening club lead, South is faced with the problem of playing spades for 5 tricks. This will only pose a problem if one defender has 4 or more spades to the ♠J.

If West has length in spades, South could pick up the spade suit by passing the ♠10 through West. This would be a poor play as it would lose to more common spade holdings with the ♠J in East's hand.

South should thus gear his play towards guarding against East being long in spades. In order to deal with East having all 5 spades, South should cash the ♠A first. When West shows out, South can finesse against East's ♠J, cross to the ♥A, and finesse again.

If West follows to the first round of spades, North wins the ♠A. Another spade is lead to the ♠K or ♠Q in South's hand. If West shows out, South can cross to the ♥A. Only 1 spade finesse is needed in this case.
